Exam Name: Screening Mammography, Bilateral with CAD

Reason for Exam / Clinical Indication:
Routine annual screening mammogram. No new breast lumps, pain, nipple discharge, or skin changes reported. Patient has no personal history of breast cancer. Family history is negative for first-degree relatives with breast cancer.

Technique:
Digital mammography was performed with two standard views (craniocaudal and mediolateral oblique) of each breast. Computer-aided detection (CAD) was utilized for image analysis.

Comparison Study:
Prior mammogram from 10/28/2023 (Evergreen Medical Center).

Findings:
BREAST COMPOSITION: The breasts are heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses.
RIGHT BREAST: No dominant masses, suspicious calcifications, or architectural distortion are identified. Skin and subcutaneous tissues appear normal.
LEFT BREAST: No dominant masses, suspicious calcifications, or architectural distortion are identified. Skin and subcutaneous tissues appear normal.
AXILLAE: No suspicious axillary lymphadenopathy is noted bilaterally.
CAD ANALYSIS: No suspicious areas were flagged by the computer-aided detection system.

Impression:
BI-RADS Category 2: Benign Finding(s).
No evidence of malignancy. Stable appearance compared to prior mammogram from 10/28/2023.

Recommendations:
Continue with routine annual screening mammography.

Electronically Signed By:
Dr. Eleanor Vance, MD
Radiologist

Date Signed: 10/26/2024 11:45

End of Report
